newsitem.title: USA: Clinton begins surgery for knee injury.
newsitem.headline: Clinton begins surgery for knee injury.

text.p: President Bill Clinton began emergency surgery on Friday to repair a torn tendon in his right knee, the White House said.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said at about 1:45 p.m. EST (1845 GMT) that Clinton had entered the operating room at the U.S. naval hospital in Bethesda, a suburb of Washington. He described Clinton as feeling occasional pain in his injured knee but in very good spirits.

McCurry, briefing reporters at the hospital, said Clinton fully intended to keep his summit date with Russian President Boris Yeltsin in Helsinki next week. "The president informed the doctors that he will be going to Helsinki on Tuesday and they said, 'yes sir,' they understood that," McCurry said.

"He's feeling very good about it (the operation) and is anxious to get it done," he said. "The president joked around with some staff and others ... He's in a little bit of pain when the leg moves but he's in very good spirits. He's joking around with a lot of us, he keeps saying he's got work to do."

Clinton caught his heel on a step at the Florida estate of Australian golfer Greg Norman early on Friday, tearing the quadriceps tendon connecting the kneecap to the upper thigh in his right leg. Doctors said the surgery was expected to last an hour or so and would probably involve use of a "regional" anaesthetic that numbs from the mid-section down, so that Clinton could remain conscious throughout.

"I think they can probably say with 90, 95 per cent surety that this can be completed without the need for a general anaesthetic," said Dr. David Wade, chief of the hospital's clinical staff who joined the briefing. McCurry added that in the unlikely event Clinton was put under full anaesthetic, procedures to temporarily shift power to Vice President Al Gore would be put into effect.
